o: Wrap a generator that yields promises so that: resolved values are sent back into the generator, rejections are thrown into it, calling cancel() before completion throws the string "Cancelled" into the generator, and the outer promise settles with the generator's return value, thrown error, or — if "Cancelled" was caught — the next yielded value or return value. If the generator finishes normally, cancel becomes a no-op.
k: Drive the generator with a recursive step function: generator.next(value) on fulfillment, generator.throw(error) on rejection.
cancel() calls generator.throw("Cancelled"); if the generator catches it and yields/returns, the outer promise follows that outcome.
Guard all in-flight promise callbacks with a cancelled flag so stale continuations never run after cancellation.

a.n: Approach 1: Recursive driver with a cancelled flag
a.i: Maintain `cancelled` and `finished` flags. A step function advances the generator, wiring each yielded promise's handlers back into step. cancel() flips the flag (silencing pending handlers), throws "Cancelled" into the generator, and settles the outer promise according to whether the generator catches it and what it yields/returns next.
s: Create the outer promise, capturing resolve/reject.
Define step(val, err, force): call generator.next/throw, settle on done, otherwise attach handlers that recurse (skipping the cancelled guard when forced).
cancel(): if already cancelled or finished, do nothing; else set cancelled, throw "Cancelled" into the generator, and settle based on the result (continuing the loop forcibly if it yields).
a.t: O(1) per yielded promise — each promise is awaited exactly once and drives one generator step.
a.sp: O(d) recursion depth where d is the number of yields (the promise chain).

w: The subtle parts: cancel must be idempotent and inert after completion; errors thrown into the generator propagate as rejections if uncaught; and after a caught cancellation the loop must resume forcibly past the cancelled flag. Test mentally against all six examples, especially example 6 (rejected yield caught by the generator, execution continues). A follow-up: support timeouts (auto-cancel after t ms).
